newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: GOLF-TORRANCE SPREAD-EAGLES FIELD AFTER LESSON FROM FATHER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TORRANCE SPREAD-EAGLES FIELD AFTER LESSON FROM FATHER.

text.p: Briton Sam Torrance, back to his best after a lesson from his father, held a six-shot lead at the midway stage of the European Masters on Friday.
Torrance took command on the Alpine course with an eight-under-par second round 63 for a total of 128.
The Scot now looks sure to collect a huge cheque which would give him a great boost in his bid for a ninth successive Ryder Cup appearance.
Torrance missed the cut at last week's British Masters, the first Ryder Cup qualifier, and went for a coaching session with his golf teacher father Bob on Monday.
"He made me move my legs and body together more and it worked," said Torrance.
"I shot 65 yesterday and 63 today and I can honestly say that these two rounds were better than any I played last year when I finished second to Monty (Colin Montgomerie) in the Order of Merit.
"Today I also went back to my normal putter. I used a heavier one yesterday and didn't feel really comfortable. So I went back to my old faithful and I had only 27 putts today."
Starting at the 10th, Torrance went out in a two-under 33 but returned in a six-under 30.
Fellow Scot Montgomerie was eight shots behind after an inconsistent 71.
Montgomerie had seven birdies but also two double bogeys and three bogeys. "It was ridiculous. I had eight birdies in my first round and seven today and I'm only six-under-par," he complained.
